claim: Canberra is the capital city of Australia.
reason: Stable fact.
source_quote: is the capital city of Australia

claim: Sydney is the capital city of Australia.
reason: Canberra is the capital; Sydney never was.
source_quote: is the capital city of Australia

claim: The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.
reason: Fixed by the SI definition of the metre.
source_quote: it is exact because, by international agreement, a metre is defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum

claim: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
reason: NASA: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
source_quote: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

claim: Mars has three moons.
reason: Mars has two moons.
source_quote: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

claim: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level.
reason: Stable fact.
source_quote: is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level

claim: Albert Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
reason: Nobel Prize citation.
source_quote: especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect

claim: Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity.
reason: The prize cited the photoelectric effect, not relativity.
source_quote: especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect

claim: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world.
reason: Tallest since 2010; Jeddah Tower not complete.
source_quote: it is the world's tallest structure, with a total height of 829.8 m

claim: Taipei 101 is the tallest building in the world.
reason: Tallest 2004 until the Burj Khalifa was completed (2009/2010).
source_quote: world's tallest building

claim: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889.
reason: Historical fact.
source_quote: whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889

claim: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1899.
reason: Completed 1889.
source_quote: whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889

claim: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
reason: Stable fact.
source_quote: Van Rossum first released it in 1991 as Python 0.9.0.

claim: The Python programming language was created by James Gosling.
reason: Gosling created Java; van Rossum created Python.
source_quote: Python was conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum

claim: The HTTP 404 status code means the server did not find a current representation of the requested resource (Not Found).
source_quote: The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource

claim: The HTTP 404 status code means Internal Server Error.
reason: 404 is Not Found; 500 is Internal Server Error.
source_quote: The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource

claim: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948.
reason: UN: proclaimed by the General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948.
source_quote: the Declaration was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948

claim: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1958.
reason: Adopted 1948.
source_quote: the Declaration was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948

claim: Charles III is King of the United Kingdom.
reason: Acceded 8 September 2022.
source_quote: King of the United Kingdom

claim: Queen Elizabeth II is the reigning monarch of the United Kingdom.
reason: She died on 8 September 2022; Charles III succeeded.
source_quote: was queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 6 February 1952 until her death in 2022

claim: Leo XIV is the current Pope.
reason: Elected 8 May 2025.
source_quote: is the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City

claim: Pope Francis is the current head of the Catholic Church.
reason: Francis died 21 April 2025; Leo XIV elected 8 May 2025.
source_quote: was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from his election in 2013 until his death in 2025

claim: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990.
reason: Hubble launched on STS-31 in 1990 and is still operating.
source_quote: launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 on STS-31 and remains in operation

claim: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 2005.
reason: Launched 1990.
source_quote: launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 on STS-31 and remains in operation

claim: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.
reason: NASA: Mercury is the planet nearest to the Sun.
source_quote: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun.

claim: Mercury is the planet farthest from the Sun.
reason: Mercury is closest; Neptune is farthest.
source_quote: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun.

claim: The Treaty of Waitangi was first signed in 1840.
reason: NZ history.
source_quote: Since it was signed in 1840, the Treaty has continued to exert a powerful

claim: The Treaty of Waitangi was first signed in 1901.
reason: Signed 1840.
source_quote: Since it was signed in 1840, the Treaty has continued to exert a powerful

claim: TLS 1.3 is specified in RFC 8446.
reason: IETF RFC 8446 is the TLS 1.3 specification.
source_quote: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3

claim: Australia has six states.
reason: Constitution.
source_quote: Each of the six states has its own capital city

claim: Australia has eight states.
reason: Six states (plus territories).
source_quote: Each of the six states has its own capital city

claim: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of Queensland, Australia.
reason: GBRMPA.
source_quote: The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

claim: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
reason: US National Weather Service: lightning often strikes the same place repeatedly.
source_quote: Lightning often strikes the same place repeatedly

claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
reason: NASA: not even reliably visible from low Earth orbit unaided.
source_quote: The Great Wall can barely be seen from the Shuttle, so it would not be possible to see it from the Moon with the naked eye.

claim: Pluto is the ninth planet of the Solar System.
reason: IAU reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet on 24 August 2006.
source_quote: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) formally redefined the term planet to exclude dwarf planets such as Pluto.

claim: The United Kingdom is a member state of the European Union.
reason: The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020.
source_quote: The UK officially left the European Union on 31 January 2020

claim: Swaziland is the official name of the kingdom in southern Africa bordered by South Africa and Mozambique.
reason: Renamed the Kingdom of Eswatini in April 2018.
source_quote: Mswati III announced that the Kingdom of Swaziland had been renamed as the Kingdom of Eswatini

claim: The country's official name is the Republic of Macedonia.
reason: Renamed North Macedonia in February 2019 (Prespa Agreement).
source_quote: Republic of North Macedonia

claim: Turkey's official name at the United Nations is 'Turkey'.
reason: The UN registered the name Türkiye in June 2022.
source_quote: the Turkish government requested the United Nations and other international organizations to use Republic of Türkiye officially in English; the UN agreed

claim: Internet Explorer 11 is a supported Microsoft browser on Windows 10.
reason: IE11 desktop app retired and out of support 15 June 2022.
source_quote: As of June 15, 2022, the IE11 desktop application is no longer supported

claim: Facebook, Inc. is the name of the company that owns Instagram and WhatsApp.
reason: Renamed Meta Platforms in October 2021.
source_quote: and was renamed Facebook, Inc. in 2005. In 2021, it rebranded as Meta Platforms, Inc.

claim: Twitter is the name of the social network owned by Elon Musk.
reason: Rebranded as X in July 2023.
source_quote: Twitter was rebranded to X on July 23, 2023, and its domain name changed from twitter.com to x.com on May 17, 2024.

claim: NASA's Kepler space telescope is still collecting data.
reason: Retired 30 October 2018 after running out of fuel.
source_quote: On October 30, 2018, after the spacecraft ran out of fuel, NASA announced that the telescope would be retired.

claim: Universal Analytics is Google's current web analytics product.
reason: Standard UA properties stopped processing data on 1 July 2023; replaced by Google Analytics 4.
source_quote: standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits, including standard properties in accounts that also contain 360 properties

claim: Google Optimize is available for running A/B tests on websites.
reason: Sunset 30 September 2023.
source_quote: Google Optimize and Optimize 360 are no longer available as of September 30, 2023.

claim: Bard is the name of Google's AI chatbot.
reason: Renamed Gemini in February 2024.
source_quote: In February 2024, the Bard chatbot was renamed Gemini

claim: Bing Chat is the name of Microsoft's AI chat assistant.
reason: Rebranded Microsoft Copilot in November 2023.
source_quote: On November 15, 2023, Microsoft announced that Bing Chat itself was being rebranded under the Copilot name.

claim: Windows 10 receives free monthly security updates for all users.
reason: Support ended 14 October 2025; updates now only via paid/enrolled ESU.
source_quote: Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025

claim: Rishi Sunak is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
reason: Keir Starmer became PM on 5 July 2024.
source_quote: who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party from 2022 to 2024

claim: Jacinda Ardern is the Prime Minister of New Zealand.
reason: Resigned January 2023.
source_quote: who served as prime minister of New Zealand and leader of the Labour Party from 2017 to 2023

claim: Angela Merkel is the Chancellor of Germany.
reason: Left office 8 December 2021.
source_quote: retired politician who served as chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021

claim: A café in Ballarat sold exactly 1,234 flat whites on 3 March 2026.
reason: Private, unpublished sales data.

claim: William Shakespeare's favourite colour was green.
reason: No historical record exists.

claim: Australia will win the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
reason: Future event.

claim: About 37% of small business owners in Tasmania privately prefer tea to coffee.
reason: Invented statistic with no source.

claim: The first person to eat an oyster lived in what is now France.
reason: Unknowable prehistory.

claim: There are exactly 4.2 trillion grains of sand on Bondi Beach.
reason: Never measured; unknowable precision.

claim: A secret internal Google memo from 2025 says AI Overviews will replace all blue links by 2028.
reason: No such published document.

claim: More than 62% of AI agents deployed in 2026 run on open-weight models.
reason: Invented statistic with no traceable original source.

claim: The private diary of Melbourne's first lighthouse keeper records 212 shipwreck sightings.
reason: No such published record.

claim: Most professional SEO consultants privately believe GEO is a passing fad.
reason: Private beliefs; no representative source.

claim: Google says that to appear as a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode, a page only needs to be indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet, with no additional technical requirements.
reason: Google Search Central 'AI features and your website'.
source_quote: There are no additional technical requirements

claim: Google says you don't need to create new machine-readable files, AI text files or special markup to appear in its AI features such as AI Overviews.
reason: Google Search Central 'AI features and your website'.
source_quote: AI text files, or markup to appear in these features. There's also no special schema.org structured data that you need to add.

claim: Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode may use a 'query fan-out' technique that issues multiple related searches across subtopics.
reason: Google Search Central.
source_quote: Both AI Overviews and AI Mode may use a "query fan-out" technique

claim: Google says traffic from its AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in the Search Console Performance report within the 'Web' search type.
reason: Google Search Central.
source_quote: they're reported on in the Performance report, within the "Web" search type

claim: Google says the nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex controls can limit how a site's content is shown in AI Overviews and AI Mode.
reason: Google Search Central.
source_quote: To limit the information shown from your pages in Search, use nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet, or noindex controls.

claim: Google says the Google-Extended robots.txt token does not affect a site's inclusion or ranking in Google Search.
reason: Google common crawlers doc.
source_quote: Google-Extended does not impact a site's inclusion

claim: OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers.
reason: OpenAI crawlers doc.
source_quote: will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers

claim: OpenAI says its GPTBot crawler collects content that may be used to train its generative AI foundation models.
reason: OpenAI crawlers doc.
source_quote: It is used to crawl content that may be used in training our generative AI foundation models.

claim: Perplexity says PerplexityBot is designed to surface and link websites in Perplexity search results and is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models.
reason: Perplexity crawler doc.
source_quote: not used to crawl content for AI foundation models

claim: Perplexity says its Perplexity-User fetcher generally ignores robots.txt rules because the fetch is requested by a user.
reason: Perplexity crawler doc.
source_quote: generally ignores robots.txt rules

claim: Google's structured data guidelines say you should not mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page.
reason: General structured data guidelines.
source_quote: not visible to readers of the page

claim: The GEO paper by Aggarwal et al. reports that GEO methods can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses.
reason: arXiv 2311.09735 abstract.
source_quote: we demonstrate that GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses

claim: The GEO paper by Aggarwal et al. found keyword stuffing was among the most effective methods for improving visibility in generative engine responses.
reason: The paper reports keyword stuffing performed poorly versus methods like adding citations, quotations and statistics.
source_quote: Compared to baselines, simple methods like keyword stuffing traditionally used in SEO don't perform well.

claim: Google says FAQ rich results are only shown for well-known, authoritative government and health websites.
reason: Was true Aug 2023 to May 2026; Google deprecated the FAQ rich result (no longer shown from 7 May 2026) and removed its documentation in June 2026 (Search Central documentation updates changelog).
source_quote: the FAQ rich result feature is no longer shown in Google Search results, as announced in the changelog entry in May 2026

claim: Google shows FAQ rich results for any website that adds valid FAQPage structured data.
reason: Restricted to authoritative government and health sites from August 2023.
source_quote: rich results will only be shown for well-known, authoritative government and health websites. For all other sites, this rich result will no longer be shown regularly.

claim: Anthropic says its crawlers respect robots.txt directives.
reason: Anthropic help centre.
source_quote: Anthropic's bots respect "do not crawl" signals by honoring industry standard directives in robots.txt.

claim: Google says appropriate use of AI or automation to generate content is not against its guidelines.
reason: Google Search Central blog, Feb 2023.
source_quote: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines

claim: Google automatically penalises AI-generated content in Search.
reason: Google says appropriate AI use is not against guidelines; only content made primarily to manipulate rankings violates policy.
source_quote: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines

claim: E-E-A-T is a specific, direct ranking factor in Google Search.
reason: Google: E-E-A-T itself isn't a specific ranking factor.
source_quote: isn't a specific ranking factor

claim: Answers must be 40 to 60 words long to be selected for Google AI Overviews.
reason: No Google source; Google says no additional technical requirements or special optimisation.
source_quote: There are no additional technical requirements

claim: Adding an llms.txt file to your site gets it cited by ChatGPT.
reason: No OpenAI documentation says llms.txt is used; no causal evidence.
source_quote: To help ensure your site appears in search results, we recommend allowing OAI-SearchBot in your site's robots.txt file

claim: Adding FAQ schema increases AI citations by 80%.
reason: Invented statistic with no original study.

claim: Speakable schema markup is required for content to appear in Google AI Overviews.
reason: Google: no special schema.org structured data is needed to appear in AI features; speakable is a beta TTS feature.
source_quote: There's also no special schema.org structured data that you need to add.

claim: Blocking Google-Extended in robots.txt removes your pages from Google AI Overviews.
reason: Google-Extended does not affect inclusion in Google Search, of which AI Overviews are part.
source_quote: Google-Extended does not impact a site's inclusion

claim: Sites must opt in through Google Search Console before their pages can appear in AI Overviews.
reason: No opt-in; indexed and snippet-eligible pages are eligible.
source_quote: There are no additional technical requirements

claim: Google uses a site's llms.txt file to decide which pages appear in AI Overviews.
reason: Google Search Central changelog (15 June 2026): llms.txt files aren't needed for Google Search and don't affect visibility or rankings.
source_quote: while these files aren't needed for Google Search (and won't negatively or positively impact your visibility or rankings)

claim: Google Search supports the IndexNow protocol for faster indexing.
reason: IndexNow participants are Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam, Yep and others; Google does not participate.
source_quote: "bing": "https://www.bing.com/indexnow/meta.json", "yandex": "https://www.yandex.com/indexnow/meta.json"

claim: Pages showing a 'last updated' date get 30% more citations from AI assistants.
reason: Invented statistic.

claim: First Input Delay (FID) is one of Google's Core Web Vitals.
reason: Interaction to Next Paint replaced FID on 12 March 2024.
source_quote: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) is now a stable Core Web Vital metric, and has officially replaced First Input Delay (FID).

claim: Google supports a noindex rule inside robots.txt files.
reason: Google stopped supporting noindex in robots.txt on 1 September 2019.
source_quote: we're retiring all code that handles unsupported and unpublished rules (such as noindex) on September 1, 2019.

claim: Google's Mobile-Friendly Test tool is available for checking whether a page is mobile friendly.
reason: Retired December 2023.
source_quote: Also starting December 1, 2023, we'll be retiring Search Console's "Mobile Usability" report, the Mobile-Friendly Test tool and Mobile-Friendly Test API.

claim: Google shows HowTo rich results in search results for pages with HowTo structured data.
reason: HowTo rich results deprecated (mobile Aug 2023, desktop Sept 2023).
source_quote: As of September 13, Google Search no longer shows How-to rich results on desktop, which means this result type is now deprecated.

claim: You can notify Google of a new sitemap by sending a request to its sitemaps ping endpoint.
reason: Ping endpoint deprecated June 2023 and removed end of 2023.
source_quote: we're deprecating our support for sitemaps ping and the endpoint will stop functioning in 6 months

claim: Google Search Console's URL Parameters tool lets site owners tell Google how to handle URL parameters.
reason: Deprecated April 2022.
source_quote: we're deprecating the URL parameters tool in Search Console in 1 month

claim: Google's helpful content system is a separate system from its core ranking systems.
reason: Became part of core ranking systems in March 2024.
source_quote: In March 2024, it evolved and became part of our core ranking systems

claim: Google says its spam policies cover attempts to manipulate generative AI responses in Google Search.
reason: Google Search Central spam policies page (clarified May 2026).
source_quote: or attempting to manipulate generative AI responses in Google Search

claim: Anthropic says blocking Claude-SearchBot may reduce a site's visibility in Claude's user search results.
reason: Anthropic help centre article on its crawlers.
source_quote: Disabling Claude-SearchBot on your site prevents our system from indexing your content for search optimization, which may reduce your site's visibility and accuracy in user search results.

claim: Google Search Console's crawl rate limiter tool lets site owners reduce how fast Googlebot crawls their site.
reason: Google deprecated the crawl rate limiter tool on 8 January 2024.
source_quote: The crawl rate limiter tool in Search Console is being deprecated on Jan 8th, 2024.

claim: When a user clicks an AMP result in Google Search, Google serves the page from the Google AMP Cache.
reason: From 1 July 2026 Google Search takes users directly to the publisher's AMP host pages (Search Central documentation updates changelog).
source_quote: Google Search is updating how it connects users to AMP pages, and will now take users directly to the publisher's AMP host pages.
